definitions.definition: For tau>0, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s)ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0, let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the decreasing rearrangement of |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|, resolving ties in any order. Nthird(a,b,c,d)=N3. Thus N3 is the second smallest of all four magnitudes including the dual output.

output.statement: For tau>0 and real alpha,beta, eta_tau(alpha,beta)=0 if alpha*beta=0; otherwise |eta_tau|<=2*min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta_tau|<=tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|). For every nonzero integer quadruple a+b+c+d=0, N1<=3*N2 and, writing A=|ab|, B0=|cd|, one has (1/|d|)*min(A/B0,B0/A)<=3/Nthird(a,b,c,d), and |a+b|/max(A,B0)<=6/Nthird(a,b,c,d).

argument.text: Fix tau,alpha,beta and assume L1: tau>0. If either phase is zero, eta=0 by the definition. Otherwise set h(s)=exp(-i*alpha*s)-M_tau(exp(-i*alpha*s)); then eta=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau h(s)exp(-i*beta*s)ds. The estimate |exp(-i*alpha*s)-exp(-i*alpha*r)|<=|alpha|*|s-r| gives |h(s)|<=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau|alpha|*|s-r|dr<=tau*|alpha|. Therefore |eta|<=tau*|alpha|, and symmetry gives tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|).

produces.statement: For the fixed tau>0 and arbitrary real alpha,beta, |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|), and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=0 if alpha*beta=0.

argument.text: More sharply, |h(0)|<=tau*|alpha|/2 and |h(tau)|<=tau*|alpha|/2 by integrating r and tau-r. Also integral_0^tau |h'(s)|ds=tau*|alpha|. Integration by parts against exp(-i*beta*s) thus gives |eta|<=(|h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral|h'|)/(tau*|beta|)<=2|alpha/beta|. Interchanging alpha,beta proves the minimum of the two ratios. The zero-phase case already settled extends the result without dividing by zero. Discharge L1.

For the frequency assertion fix integers a,b,c,d and assume L2: abcd!=0 and a+b+c+d=0. The triangle inequality gives N1<=3*N2. Put A=|ab| and B0=|cd|. If d is among the largest two, min(A/B0,B0/A)/|d|<=1/N3. Otherwise the largest two are among a,b,c. If they are a,b, bound the minimum by B0/A and obtain |c|/|ab|<=1/N3. If they are a,c, their ratio is between 1/3 and 3; the remaining sizes |b|,|d| have maximum N3. Hence the expression is <=3*min(|b|/|d|^2,1/|b|)<=3/max(|b|,|d|)=3/N3. The b,c case is identical after exchanging a,b. Ties may be ordered arbitrarily and these alternatives still cover them.

For the second majorant, use the pairing (a,b),(c,d). If the largest two are in the same pair, the other pair has sum <=2*N3, while max(A,B0)>=N1*N2. Since a+b=-(c+d), |a+b|/max(A,B0)<=2*N3/(N1*N2)<=2/N3. If the largest two are in different pairs, the third largest is paired with one of them, so max(A,B0)>=N2*N3; also |a+b|<=2*N1<=6*N2. The quotient is <=6/N3. Discharge L2 and universally quantify; together with the first two paragraphs this proves the asserted conclusion.
